title: Model admittance heuristics & rollback playbook
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a proposed set of heuristics and an operational rollback playbook for admitting new model variants (and kernel/quantization variants) into our serving plane when speculative decoding is enabled. Goal is to minimize user-visible regressions while allowing rapid rollouts of performance improvements (kernels, quantized variants, KV lease tuning) and to give SREs/runbook authors a concise, actionable rollback path when regressions appear.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to new model variants (same architecture, diff weights or quantization) and to kernel/runtime patchsets that change path selection for speculative decoding.
- Assumes existing traffic routing supports canary percentages and header-based routing.
- Relies on runtime telemetry we already emit: per-model p50/p95 latency, token throughput, KV cache hit ratio (prefix hit & KV reuse), token-cost estimate, error-rate (API 5xx/4xx), and token-level divergence probes (see metrics section).
- Does NOT cover database migration or infra-only patches. Separate playbooks for infra changes.

High-level admittance heuristics (quick summary):
1) Start in isolated canary at 0.5-1% traffic with 100% deterministic routing of test sets for quality probes.
2) Run for N minutes (default 30m) and collect: latency, tail latency, token-cost delta, KV-hit delta, and quality probes (prompt set).
3) Scoring: compute a rolling admission score from weighted deltas. Accept if score above threshold and no hard failure triggers.
4) Gradual ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with hold windows at each stage. Each stage requires passing both safety gates and quality gates.

Detailed acceptance gates:
- Safety gates (must pass):
  - Error rate change (5xx+4xx) relative increase < 0.2% absolute or < 20% relative, whichever is smaller.
  - P95 latency increase < 30ms absolute AND < 10% relative (configurable per SLA class).
  - KV-cache prefix hit ratio not decreased by more than 3 percentage points for the same workload slice.
  - Memory / GPU OOM events: zero allowed.

- Quality gates (probabilistic):
  - Prompt-set BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity on canary prompts: median delta within tolerance (default: cosine similarity > 0.985) and < 1.5% of prompts flagged as below tolerance.
  - Token-level divergence probes: measured using deterministic replay of 500 short prompts; divergence rate < 0.5% for top-1 outputs.

- Cost/perf gates (to allow performance improvements rather than regressions):
  - Token-cost delta must be <= +5% (we allow small cost rises if quality improves), or if cost decreases >3% that is a positive signal.
  - Batchable throughput: observed tokens/sec must be >= baseline * 0.95 for same sequence distribution at steady state.

Admission scoring model (operational simple formula):
- Each metric mapped to a normalized score in [-1.0, +1.0] (negative = regression). Weights: quality(0.45), safety(0.25), latency(0.15), cost(0.10), kv(0.05).
- Composite score = sum(weight * normalized_metric). Threshold to progress: >= 0.3. If 0.0 < score < 0.3 then hold and extend observation window. If score <= 0.0 -> rollback immediately.
- Rationale: quality has priority because small latency wins are bad if outputs degrade.

Kernel oscillation & routing stability heuristics:
Problem: frequent kernel path changes (e.g., fallbacks between quantized/unquantized kernels during speculative decoding) can cause oscillation and KV-staleness.
Mitigations:
- Sticky kernel assignment for a request family: once a request stream (client session id or trace id) is assigned a kernel variant, keep assignment stable for N requests or T seconds (default: 300s or 10 requests).
- Backoff on rapid kernel-flip: if an endpoint flips kernel selection > 3 times in 60s for the same batch characteristics, throttle speculative probing and prefer conservative kernel for that slice.
- KV lease cohesion: when kernel assignment changes, KV lease for that model variant must be refreshed and previous KV entries marked with 'stale-variant-id' tag; runtime must refuse cross-variant KV reuse unless explicit compatibility bit is set for the variant pair.

KV lease semantics and safety:
- Two-level KV lease: short lease (soft) for speculative prefixes (30-60s) and long lease (hard) for confirmed prefixes (5-15m).
- When admitting a new variant, do NOT reuse long-lease KV entries from prior variant unless:
  1) model variant reports bitwise-compatible KV schema (rare)
  2) there is a validated compatibility flag on the model manifest
- On rollback we must invalidate KV entries touched by the new variant: runtime should support a 'variant-invalidate' RPC that marks all KV keys with variant id X as invalid (async background eviction).

Rollback playbook (operational checklist):
Immediate detection triggers (auto-rollback candidates):
- Composite admission score <= 0.0 observed at any hold stage.
- Error-rate jump: >= 0.5% absolute increase OR 3x relative increase for critical customers.
- P95 latency regression > 100ms absolute for customer-tiered SLO.
- Quality probe failure: > 3% of critical prompt-set queries failing similarity threshold.

Manual rollback steps (for SRE / oncall):
1) Pause rollout: set routing weight to 0% for the canary variant. (JIRA-INF-4219)
2) If canary already at >5% and customer-impacting, immediately route traffic to previous stable variant and set an incident signal.
3) Trigger variant-invalidate KV RPC for the admitted variant id (async).
4) Disable speculative kernel probing for the affected model until the next safe admission window.
5) Open a postmortem note: record observed deltas, logs (kernel switch traces), and example failing prompts. Attach to the rollout PR.
6) If rollback was due to kernel oscillation, raise a 'kernel-stickiness' config update and schedule a short patch to increase sticky window.

Post-rollback validation:
- Confirm error rates & latencies return to baseline within 10 minutes for majority of traffic.
- Check KV invalidation progress: prefix hit ratio should trend back to baseline after background eviction completes.
- Re-run deterministic prompt-set on stable variant to verify prior quality.

Operational metrics to surface & alerts to configure:
- Admission composite score (per-variant), emitted every minute
- P50/P95/P99 latency deltas (per-variant, per-route)
- KV prefix-hit ratio and KV-variant-hit ratio (fraction of hits from same variant)
- Token divergence probes: fraction of prompts with token mismatch at top-1
- Kernel-flip rate: flips per minute per server
- Token-cost-per-request delta (estimated)
- Error rate delta (4xx/5xx)

Alert thresholds (examples):
- PAGE: error-rate delta >= 0.5% OR p95 delta >= 100ms for premium routes
- SEV-2: composite score <= 0.0 for two consecutive windows (5m)
- SEV-3: kernel-flip rate > 3/minute/server for 3 minutes

Telemetry implementation notes (for infra/metrics team):
- Emit variant-id in all traces and in KV telemetry.
- When storing KV, tag with variant-id and lease-type (soft/long).
- Add a dedicated small deterministic probe job that replays 500 seed prompts against the canary every 5 minutes and emits similarity metrics. Keep probe traffic separate from production routing but use the same runtime paths.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How strictly to prevent KV reuse between close quantized variants (wastes cache but safer). Leaning conservative for now.
- Should we allow per-customer whitelist for aggressive models (customers opt-in to early access)? Proposal: yes, via routing headers, with stricter customer-level SLO monitoring.
- Do we want rollback to also trigger automatic GitHub PR revert? Risky — prefer human in loop for PR reverts.

Action items / next steps:
- Add variant-invalidate RPC (infra) — owner: Marco — due 2024-11-20.
- Add composite admission score to the metrics pipeline and Grafana dashboard — owner: Evelyn — due 2024-11-27.
- Implement sticky-kernel assignment + config knobs — owner: Samir — prototype by 2024-12-08.
- Run 3 canary rollouts with these heuristics on non-critical models and collect telemetry for tuning.

Appendix: example admission timeline for a hypothetical rollout
- 00:00: Create canary at 1% traffic (deterministic probe traffic included).
- 00:30: Composite score = 0.45 (good). Ramp to 5%
- 01:30: Composite score = 0.32, but p95 delta = +28ms (within gate). Ramp to 20%
- 03:10: Composite score drops to -0.12 due to kernel-flip bursts and token divergence = 0.8% -> Immediate rollback triggered -> route to previous stable variant, invalidate KV entries.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative on KV reuse to avoid subtle quality regressions. Recommend we iterate the weights in the admission score after trying 3-5 real canaries.
- Feedback welcome: particularly from UX/console teams on how to surface composite score and rollback actions in the Console UI.

End of doc.
